text: a minimal model of Theorem 3 with six hidden states

chain.link: Main §2.4 is titled "A Minimal Model" and ch01:135 "A worked minimal model"; neither states a measure nor proves minimality. Corpus-wide search (papers/, book/, OIBridge, verification/) finds no minimality statement or proof for this model.

Refuted under hidden-state count: (i) a 2-hidden-state model realizes Theorem 3 (the card game; exhaustive: 16 of 24 bijections at |C_V| = |C_H| = 2 with uniform prior); (ii) a 3-hidden-state model (h = 1 flips x; h = 2 ↔ 3 swap) reproduces every B.1 number exactly: Γ_1 = [[2/3,1/3],[1/3,2/3]], Γ_2 = I, divisor [[2,−1],[−1,2]], conditionals 1 and 1/3; at |C_V| = 2, |C_H| = 3 all 648 Theorem-3 witnesses have invertible Γ_s, so even the "unique divisor with negative entries" feature needs only 3 hidden states (2 with a non-uniform prior, e.g. φ(x,h) = (x ⊕ h, h) with P(h=1) ≠ 1/2).

text: a two-card game, the smallest realization of Theorem 3

chain.link: Measure and proof (supplied by this audit; absent from the corpus): a realization of Theorem 3 needs two distinct rows (|C_V| ≥ 2) and an overlap; with |C_H| = 1 the step is a permutation of C_V, so every Γ_t is a permutation matrix and no two distinct rows overlap; hence |C_V| ≥ 2 and |C_H| ≥ 2, and s ≥ 1 (Γ_0 = I has no overlap) so n ≥ 2. The card game attains |C_V| = |C_H| = 2, s = 1, n = 2.

text: The two-card game of [Book §1.11] uses two cards, each red or black: a visible *hole card* $h$, and a face-down *burn card* $b$, uniform and independent of $h$.
